issues.legal_issue: Concurrent factual findings based on accepted eyewitness evidence should not be displaced when the alternative account of an attack in self-defence is unsupported by the circumstances.
material_facts: Both lower courts accepted the eyewitness evidence describing the assault at the well.
The accused who admitted being present claimed that the deceased and others had attacked them there and that the deaths resulted from blows struck by members of the deceased persons’ own group.
The alleged attacking group was larger, yet its members suffered two deaths and several injuries while only two accused had very minor injuries.
There was no evidentiary basis for a recent provocation that would explain the alleged group attack.
issues.conclusion: The Supreme Court accepted the concurrent findings about the well incident and rejected the defence account as false.
issues.legal_principle: The Court found no sufficient reason to disturb the concurrent assessment of the eyewitness evidence. It considered the comparative injuries and absence of a recent provocative cause in assessing the plausibility of the self-defence account. No earlier cases or specific statutory provisions were relied on for this conclusion.

rule.if: criminal_appeal and concurrent_witness_findings and alleged_attack_group_larger and accused_injuries_minor and no_recent_provocation

predicates.criminal_appeal: The case is a criminal appeal challenging findings made after trial.
predicates.concurrent_witness_findings: The trial court and the appellate court accepted eyewitness evidence describing the incident.
predicates.alleged_attack_group_larger: The defence account required the accused to have faced a group larger than their own.
predicates.accused_injuries_minor: The accused suffered only minor injuries in the incident.
predicates.no_recent_provocation: The evidence did not identify a recent cause for the alleged attack by the opposing group.

issues.definition: When a criminal appeal challenges concurrent eyewitness findings, and the alleged group attack is unsupported by the relative injuries and any recent provocation, the prosecution account is accepted.

issues.legal_issue: A common intention need not be formed by a prior plan, but liability for a particular result requires a shared intention to bring about that result rather than merely simultaneous independent intentions.
material_facts: The three accused jointly began beating two workers with spear handles and a stick.
When the deceased intervened, one accused struck him on the legs, another stabbed him near the ear, and the third stabbed him in the jaw.
The jaw wound caused the fatal brain injury, while the other accused’s blows did not cause the fatal injury.

The sequence, targeted body parts, and effects of the blows did not establish a shared intention to kill, but the three had a shared intention to beat the deceased with weapons likely to cause grievous injuries.
issues.conclusion: The three accused shared an intention to beat the deceased with weapons likely to cause grievous injuries, but they did not share an intention to kill him. All three were therefore guilty of grievous hurt under Section 326 read with Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code, while the two accused other than the fatal stabber could not be convicted of murder on the basis of common intention.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code, a prior concert or distinct previous plan is not necessary; a common intention may develop on the spot. Whether participants shared an intention to bring about a particular result, rather than acting with simultaneous independent intentions, depends on the facts. The Court applied Sections 34, 326 and 302 of the Indian Penal Code and cited no earlier cases.

rule.if: joint_assault_case and shared_intention_to_beat and weapons_likely_to_cause_grievous_injury and no_shared_intention_to_kill

predicates.joint_assault_case: The case concerns multiple accused who jointly assaulted a victim.
predicates.shared_intention_to_beat: The participants shared an intention to beat the victim.
predicates.weapons_likely_to_cause_grievous_injury: The participants used weapons likely to cause grievous injuries.
predicates.no_shared_intention_to_kill: The circumstances do not establish a shared intention among the participants to kill the victim.

issues.definition: When participants jointly assault a victim with a shared intention to beat him using weapons likely to cause grievous injury, but do not share an intention to kill him, they are liable for grievous hurt rather than murder by common intention.

issues.legal_issue: An accused who deliberately inflicts the fatal injury on a helpless victim is individually liable for murder even when the other participants did not share an intention to kill.
material_facts: One accused stabbed the deceased in the jaw with a spear while the deceased was lying on the ground.
The wound penetrated the skull and injured the brain, and the medical evidence identified it as the cause of death.
The stabber placed his legs on the deceased’s chest and extracted the spear blade from the wound.
The Court found the act brutal and fatal and inferred a deliberate intention to finish the deceased, rather than an accidental act.
issues.conclusion: The accused who inflicted the fatal spear wound was guilty of murder under Section 302 of the Indian Penal Code, and his murder conviction was maintained.
issues.legal_principle: The Court applied Section 302 of the Indian Penal Code to the accused’s own fatal act. It inferred intention from the nature and effect of the wound and the circumstances in which it was inflicted; no earlier cases were cited.

rule.if: criminal_homicide_case and accused_inflicted_fatal_wound and victim_helpless_when_wounded and deliberate_fatal_attack

predicates.criminal_homicide_case: The case concerns an accused charged in connection with a victim’s death.
predicates.accused_inflicted_fatal_wound: The accused personally inflicted the wound that caused the victim’s death.
predicates.victim_helpless_when_wounded: The victim was lying on the ground and helpless when the wound was inflicted.
predicates.deliberate_fatal_attack: The circumstances of the attack showed that the fatal wound was deliberately inflicted rather than caused accidentally.

issues.definition: When an accused personally and deliberately inflicts the fatal wound on a helpless victim, the accused is liable for murder.

issues.legal_issue: A conviction for causing simple injuries in a joint assault may be maintained where the participants shared an intention to beat the injured persons.
material_facts: The three accused jointly beat two workers with spear handles and a stick.
The workers sustained injuries that the medical evidence classified as simple.
The Court found that the accused shared an intention to beat the workers.
issues.conclusion: The convictions of all three accused under Section 323 of the Indian Penal Code for assaulting the two workers were maintained.
issues.legal_principle: The Court applied Section 323 of the Indian Penal Code to the simple injuries caused in the joint assault. It found a shared intention to beat the workers; no earlier cases were cited.

predicates.joint_assault_case: The case concerns multiple accused who jointly assaulted victims.
predicates.shared_intention_to_beat_injured_people: The participants shared an intention to beat the injured people.
predicates.injuries_simple: The injuries caused to the people who were beaten were medically classified as simple.

issues.definition: When participants jointly beat people with a shared intention to do so and the resulting injuries are simple, the participants are convicted of causing simple injuries.

issues.legal_issue: A death sentence may be maintained when the accused deliberately inflicts a brutal, fatal attack on a helpless victim in circumstances showing a pre-existing motive.
material_facts: The accused inflicted a brutal and fatal spear wound on the deceased while he was lying helpless on the ground.
The Court considered that the accused was actuated by pre-existing enmity and intended to finish the deceased.
The High Court had imposed a death sentence, and the Supreme Court found no reason to disagree with it.
issues.conclusion: The death sentence imposed on the accused was maintained.
issues.legal_principle: The Court found no reason to interfere with the sentence in light of the deliberate, brutal and fatal nature of the attack and the circumstances indicating motive. It cited no statutory provision or earlier case in reaching this sentencing conclusion.

predicates.criminal_sentencing_case: The case involves review of a sentence imposed following a criminal conviction.
predicates.deliberate_brutal_fatal_attack_on_helple: The offender deliberately inflicted a brutal fatal attack while the victim was helpless.
predicates.pre_existing_motive: The circumstances showed that the offender acted from a motive that existed before the attack.

issues.definition: When sentencing review concerns a deliberate, brutal fatal attack on a helpless victim and the circumstances show a pre-existing motive, the death sentence is maintained.
